summary: A rural mountain outing east of Chiang Mai built around Mae Kampong village and its forest waterfall, with San Kamphaeng Hot Springs on the approach and Kew Fin viewpoint as an optional highland spur. Plan this as a driver-led out-and-back unless local authorities confirm the through-road is open; the evidence available does not establish a dependable full loop for December 2026.
whyGo: See a forested highland village and a seven-tier waterfall in one trip from Chiang Mai.
Add a hot-spring soak near the start or end of the drive; the official tourism listing describes pools, foot baths and private bathing rooms.
Kew Fin offers a higher viewpoint and possible morning cloud views when weather and access cooperate.
bestFor: Travellers with a full day, flexible timing and a driver familiar with narrow mountain roads.
Visitors who want rural scenery and community tourism more than a strenuous hike.
Groups happy to make the viewpoint optional and adapt to road or weather conditions.
skipIf: You need a guaranteed through-loop, fixed arrival time or frequent public transport.
You are uncomfortable with steep, winding roads, tight village streets or uneven waterfall paths.
You need step-free access throughout; village and waterfall paths are not documented as accessible.
duration: Allow 7–9 hours from Chiang Mai as a planning estimate, including roughly 1–1.5 hours each way to Mae Kampong, the hot springs, village and waterfall stops, and road delays. Add time for Kew Fin; skip it if the local access road is closed or slow. A Chiang Mai–Mae Kampong–Kew Fin–Chae Son circuit should be attempted only after confirming the connecting road is open that day.
cost: Variable. Transport/driver, meals and any community waterfall or parking fees are additional. The Japan National Tourism Organization's Chiang Mai listing reports San Kamphaeng Hot Springs admission ฿100 plus ฿65 for hot-spring use, with child rates half price; reconfirm these older listed rates before travel. No current Kew Fin charge was verified.
hours: Mae Kampong village has no single verified opening schedule. The Ministry of Tourism and Sports directory lists the waterfall as open 24 hours but notes hours can change; a current local visitor guide gives 08:00–17:00 and recommends paying the community fee. Treat daylight hours as the practical limit. San Kamphaeng Hot Springs is listed as 07:00–18:00; confirm before setting out.
bestTime: Start early, especially for Kew Fin, cooler air and a better chance of cloud views. December is in northern Thailand's cooler, generally drier season, but mountain temperatures, mist and visibility vary by day; no December 2026 forecast exists yet.
gettingThere: From Chiang Mai, travel east via San Kamphaeng and Mae On toward Huai Kaeo and Mae Kampong (about 1–1.5 hours to the village per the local visitor guide). A private car with an experienced driver is the most practical way to combine stops. The hot springs have a listed Chiang Mai minivan service, but that does not provide onward village/viewpoint connections. The final roads are winding and narrow; arrange return pickup and check whether the Mae Kampong–Kew Fin/Chae Son road is open before choosing a circuit.
booking: No general advance booking requirement for a day visit was found. Reserve a driver for the full day in advance during December and agree the itinerary, waiting time, return plan and any extra charge for Kew Fin. Confirm hot-spring services and community waterfall access locally shortly before departure.
accessibility: The road reaches the village, but its compact streets and waterfall nature trail may include steep slopes, steps and uneven surfaces. Kew Fin access is a mountain roadside viewpoint and terrain/access details are not confirmed. Hot springs list pools and foot baths, but full step-free access and accessible changing facilities were not verified.
practicalTips: Ask your driver to verify the through-road with local authorities or the village before departure; default to returning the way you came.
Park only in designated spaces and follow local signs and community fee requests in Mae Kampong.
Wear shoes with grip for the waterfall path, carry cash and water, and bring a light layer for the high ground.
Keep the viewpoint optional: mist, low cloud, roadworks or holiday congestion can make it a poor addition.
Avoid driving the narrow mountain roads after dark and allow extra time around holiday weekends.
decemberNotes: The TMD describes December–January as the coolest period in northern Thailand, and its 2024 monthly summary recorded a 4°C reading on a Chiang Mai mountaintop during December. That is an example, not a forecast for Mae On. Cool mornings, mist and reduced visibility are plausible; waterfalls may have less flow than in the wet season. December 2026 roadworks, viewpoint access and facility hours remain unverified, so confirm locally in the days before the trip.
uncertainties: A currently open, all-weather through-road connecting Mae Kampong, Kew Fin and Chae Son was not verified; this determines whether a true loop is practical.
The local visitor guide is not an official authority and its hours, fees, route and difficulty details may change.
Current transport prices, community waterfall fees, Kew Fin access/charges and December 2026 closures are not confirmed.
Cloud-view probability, waterfall flow and road conditions on a specific December day cannot be predicted yet.
